expect.note: each check is (model submitted, HTTP status, model the planner factory received)

provenance: M9 introduced a `model` field on POST /tasks so the ablation driver can vary the planner from outside the deployment. The endpoint is public and unauthenticated, and OpenRouter bills whatever model id it is handed — so before the guard existed, any stranger could point this deployment's key at the most expensive model on the platform, one request at a time, and the run budgets (30 actions / 100k tokens) would not notice because they count tokens, not price. Watched red before any of it existed: with no `model` field on `TaskIn`, Pydantic drops unknown keys silently, so all five rows — including the empty string and the path-traversal one — returned HTTP 200 with a run_id and a run that started. Nothing refused anything; the endpoint simply did not look. Rows refreshed at the owner's model-set change (2026-08-20). Row 1 is now `anthropic/claude-opus-5` — leaderboard top-10 and the model the owner named as the thing not to use — so the case refuses the concrete expensive model somebody would actually reach for, not a hypothetical. Row 2 is a real variant suffix on an allowlisted id, the shape a `startswith` check lets through; row 3 the same id with a trailing space.

triage.note: tagged invariant — a public endpoint that spends money on an unbounded caller-supplied parameter must always be gated, not gated-at-the-baseline. Refusal is 422 with a `model blocked` detail, the same shape and status the URL guard's refusal uses, so the frontend's existing rejection path renders it with no change. The endpoint gates on `ALLOWED_MODELS` (the four ablated ids plus the incumbent default), not on `ABLATION_MODELS`: the default must stay reachable by explicit name even though it is priced out of the comparison. Rows 2, 3 and 4 are the near-misses: an allowlisted id with a trailing space, which a `startswith` or substring check would let through, and the empty string, which a truthiness-guarded `if t.model and ...` would silently treat as 'not specified' and run on the default. Membership is tested against `is not None`, so only an ABSENT field defaults; a present-but-empty one is a caller sending something, and something not on the list is refused.

provenance_m42_2026_08_26: The refused-frontier-model row moved from `anthropic/claude-opus-5` to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` because M42 added the former to ALLOWED_MODELS as loop mode's declared, price-recorded exception (ADR-027 Decision 4, ADR-028). The row's POINT is unchanged and is why it is not simply deleted: this endpoint is public and unauthenticated, OpenRouter bills whatever id it is handed, and an expensive frontier model that nobody allowlisted must still be refused before a run exists. Watched red when the allowlist widened and this file still named the newly-accepted id: `{model: anthropic/claude-opus-5, want {http: 422}, got {http: 200, planner_model: anthropic/claude-opus-5}}` — the allowlist and its own refusal case disagreeing, which is exactly what this case exists to make impossible to miss.
